{{nihongo|'''Hoshi Shrine'''|星神社 (名古屋市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kamiotai|ja|上小田井|qid=Q11358809}}, {{ill|Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Q1207973|qid=Q1207973|lt=Nishi Ward}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is considered a candidate shrine for "Sakaniwa Shrine" of Yamada District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}. {{nihongo|'''Hoshi Shrine'''|星神社 (名古屋市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== History ==
The founding date is unknown<ref name="meikan"/>. Shrine tradition says it was established in the Ninna era by descendants of {{ill|Ōe no Otondo|ja|大江音人|qid=Q11436894}} living near this area. War fires burned the shrine buildings along with treasures, sacred objects, and writings about shrine origins<ref name="meikan"/>. It is said to have once had shrine lands of 4 chō 8 tan, but these were confiscated in the time of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}. One theory says the former site was around present {{ill|Sakaido-chō|Q38277934|qid=Q38277934}}. {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40), it became a designated village shrine<ref name="meikan"/>.

Since the Edo period, the shrine side has claimed it is the Yamada District "Sakaniwa Shrine" listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō<ref name="meikan"/>. ''Owari-shi'' cites as evidence a Genroku-era report by shrine official Aoki Shinano-no-kami that wrote "Sakaniwa Hoshinomiya"{{Sfn|Nagoya Local Culture Society|1987|p=1}}. It also mentions an old secret text from the Kanpyō era written "Sakaniwa Hoshi no Miya"{{Sfn|Nagoya Local Culture Society|1987|p=1}}, though its reliability is unclear.

Yamada District's "Sakaniwa Shrine" was identified by {{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} with Sannō Myōjin of Sakaba village (the present {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sakaniwa Shrine}} in {{ill|Komaki|Q389537|qid=Q389537}}), and that became standard theory{{Efn|Because the place name Sakaba resembles Sakaniwa, the shrine called Sannō Myōjin in Sakaba village was identified as Sakaniwa Shrine. The current Sakaniwa Shrine in Komaki was renamed from Sannō Myōjin based on this theory{{Sfn|Nagoya Local Culture Society|1987|p=2}}.}}. However, Komaki clearly lay in {{ill|Kasugai district|ja|春日井郡|pl|Powiat Kasugai|zh|春日井郡|qid=Q11513576}} rather than Yamada District, so it is not considered a strong candidate for the original "Sakaniwa Shrine."

== Other ==
The three {{ill|Aphananthe aspera|Q4779482|qid=Q4779482}} near the front entrance were designated on February 27, {{ill|1995|Q2068|qid=Q2068}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 7) as Nagoya's {{ill|Important Urban Landscape Buildings, etc.|Q11415135|qid=Q11415135}} (urban landscape preservation trees)<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.city.nagoya.jp/kankou/category/358-1-0-0-0-0-0-0-0-0.html|title=Nagoya City: designated important urban landscape buildings etc.|publisher=Nagoya City|work=Housing and Urban Development Bureau, Cityscape Office|date=2012-09-25|accessdate=2012-11-15}}</ref>. The largest is about 18 m tall with trunk circumference over 4 m.

At the honden completion dedication ceremony held on the night of {{ill|November 12|Q2986|qid=Q2986}}, {{ill|2019|Q25274|qid=Q25274}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|ar|فترة رييوا|az|Reyva erası|ban|Reiwa|be|Рэйва|bo|རེ་བ|bug|ᨑᨙᨕᨗᨓ|ca|Període Reiwa|cdo|Lêng-huò|cs|Období Reiwa|de|Reiwa-Zeit|eo|Reiva-epoko|es|Era Reiwa|fa|دوره ریوا|fi|Reiwa-kausi|fr|Ère Reiwa|haw|Reiwa Makahiki|he|תקופת ראיווה|hi|रेइवा युग|hu|Reiva-kor|id|Zaman Reiwa|it|Periodo Reiwa|ja|令和|jv|Reiwa|ka|რეივა|ko|레이와 시대|lt|Reiva laikotarpis|mn|Рэйва|ms|Zaman Reiwa|nl|Reiwa|no|Reiwa|oc|Reiwa|pl|Reiwa|pt|Período Reiwa|ro|Perioada Reiwa|ru|Рэйва|simple|Reiwa era|sk|Obdobie Reiwa|sl|Obdobje Reiva|sq|Periudha Reiva|sv|Reiwa|th|ยุคเรวะ|tr|Reiwa Dönemi|uk|Період Рейва|uz|Reiva|vi|Thời kỳ Lệnh Hòa|wuu|令和|zh|令和|zh_classical|令和|zh_min_nan|Lēng-hô|zh_yue|令和|qid=Q62609017}} 1), {{ill|Mieko Hirota|Q3543602|qid=Q3543602}} offered a song rendition of "When You Wish Upon a Star"; to commemorate this, a stone monument noting it was placed in the precincts.
